According to the Brønsted–Lowry model, acid–base chemistry encompasses a broad range of reactions in which protons are donated by species called the acid and accepted by species called the base. These reactions play key roles in situations that include industrial manufacturing processes, ordinary household substances, and the life-sustaining reactions in living systems. In aqueous solutions, all acids and bases react with the water in which they are dissolved. An acid increases the concentration of the hydronium ion H3O1 above its value in pure water, which is controlled by the ion product constant of water. A base increases the concentration of the hydroxide ion OH2 above the value it takes in pure water, due to the ion product constant of water. The concentration of the hydronium ion is conveniently expressed by pH, and that of the hydroxide by pOH. These quantities are related as pH 1 pOH 5 14 by the ion product constant of water. Some acids and bases dissociate completely in solution to produce concentrations of hydronium and hy- droxide equivalent to the concentration of parent acid or base with which the solu- tions were prepared.
